fact_text: A REIT pools money from many investors, from small to large, and invests it in income-producing or developing real estate, so its units work much like mutual fund units.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: A REIT that distributes its rental income to unit holders gets pass-through tax status, the same idea as a mutual fund that pays out about 90 percent of its income as dividends.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: Under SECP rules a REIT first sells units by private placement to credited, high-net-worth investors and must list within three years, after which the general public can buy units.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: Once listed, a REIT unit can be bought with as little as about PKR 5,000 to 10,000, while private placement has no set minimum but is usually sized for credited investors.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: Pakistan's first listed REIT, Dolmen REIT, came around mid-2015, and restrictive rules kept REIT management companies from launching new REITs until the 2022 regulations increased activity.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: Three REITs were listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange and more than 10 were available through private placement, according to the interview as of 10 Aug 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: The guest put the combined market capitalisation of Pakistan's listed REITs at roughly USD 240 to 250 million, with both figures given in the interview as of 10 Aug 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: Singapore's REIT market was cited at about USD 73 billion, while India and Malaysia were each put at roughly USD 10 to 12 billion, as regional comparisons in the interview.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: Capitalisation rates on residential and commercial property were cited as roughly 2 to 8 percent, and the guest said a working-space REIT could reach a dividend yield of about 10 percent.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: The guest projected dividend yields of 10 to 12 percent for the hotel REIT project in Hyderabad once the hotel becomes operational, with property value gains also paid out as dividends.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: The hotel REIT case rests on strong demand in Hyderabad with little supply of rooms for corporate visitors, who often have to stay in guest houses when hotels are fully booked.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: The hotel REIT was pitched on two returns: land appreciation in secondary cities, which the guest said has not risen as much as in major cities, and rental income from room rates passed to investors.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: An operating hotel REIT is an ongoing business, so unlike residential or office projects that rely on an exit by sale, it can have a perpetual life, the guest said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: Section 99 tax treatment for REITs was removed in 2023, and the guest said its restoration is needed so that non-cash REIT real estate transfers are not taxed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: Withholding taxes and gaps in pass-through exemptions create problems for REIT management companies and their investors, which the guest said discourages institutional and individual investors.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: The guest said Pakistan's savings rate has fallen below 4 percent, and unregulated real estate investments lead people to lose money that regulated REITs could help protect.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: The guest said public-private partnerships for large projects such as roads and flyovers could be carried through REITs, a regulated vehicle that could help fund the infrastructure the country needs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: The guest argued that a REIT lets savers share in property price growth, which outpaces earnings growth and inflation, instead of having to buy a home outright.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)

fact_text: REITs are increasingly used in developing countries for data centres and solar power plants, where most of the income comes from real estate related assets.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Invest in Real Estate with PKR 5,000: REITs Explained | Pakistan Property Playbook | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-10)
